text:
Maria: Heads up — our eu-west canary pool that was migrated to CUDA 12 this morning is showing provisioning failures and a ton of image rebuilds. Nodes are cycling during startup.
Ajay: Noted, seeing the same from the autoscaler metrics. Provisioning latency jumped from ~30s to 4-5m and some pods keep OOMing on init.
Kai: Any modprobe or kernel errors in the node logs?
Maria: Pasted the last lines from one node: `modprobe: FATAL: Module nvidia not found in directory /lib/modules/5.15.0-1029-azure` then systemd tries to start kubelet -> containerd -> crashes with `error initializing NVML: driver/library version mismatch`.
SRE-Oncall: infra-bot flagged >20 nodes with "driver+toolkit mismatch". I've quarantined 5 nodes from the canary pool to prevent autoscaler from reusing them.
infra-bot: [alert] 1967894332 - driver-toolkit-mismatch detected on nodes: euw-canary-{12..31}. Action recommended: cordon -> drain -> reprovision.
Ajay: That NVML message indicates the kernel driver and userland toolkit are out of sync. Did the image rebuild reorder libcuda symlinks or strip ABI symbols?
Maria: Build pipeline did a full container rebuild to pick up toolkit 12.0.1 artifacts. We pinned the base image to debian-12 but didn't pin libgcc/libstdc++.
Kai: We haven't rebuilt dkms nvidia modules for the new kernel ABI on these nodes. Some nodes are still on kernel 5.15, others on 6.x due to rolling kernel updates in the cloud image. Bad combo.
Lisa: I saw NCCL errors earlier: `NCCL WARN No p2p support for interconnect: peer access disabled`. Might be a userland/driver mismatch too. Also noticed `tc qdisc` complaining in the logs — network stack flapping during heavy pod churn.
Ajay: Network flapping + repeated container rebuilds = pressure on kubelet and cgroups, which can increase OOMs. Autoscaler then spins up more nodes -> more mismatched kernels -> more failures. Feedback loop and cost spike.
Maria: Cost alert already fired — 3x expected capacity in eu-west for the canary for ~40min. Raising to ops lead.
SRE-Oncall: Temporary mitigation plan: 1) Pause autoscaler for eu-west canary, 2) Blacklist images with bare `:latest` toolkit tag, 3) Roll clusters that have kernel 6.x back to the stable 5.15 gold image where drivers were rebuilt successfully.
Kai: Agreed. Also we should add a preflight hook to the rebuild job that checks `modinfo nvidia` and `nvidia-smi` inside a warm node in a staging pool before promoting the image.
Lisa: Can we do a fallback to the pre-toolkit12 image for any pending jobs? Some scheduled training jobs are failing overnight.
Ajay: I've queued a rollback for the image tag `redwood/serve:cu11-stable-2026-03-18` and updated node taints so the failing pods won't reschedule onto new toolkit12 nodes.
Maria: How widespread is this? Only eu-west canary or other regions?
infra-bot: [scan] 1967894400 - Detected toolkit mismatch risk in eu-west and ap-southeast canary pools. us-central seems OK (still on toolkit 11.x).
Kai: ap-southeast had a different kernel cadence; might be fine but let's treat as at-risk.
SRE-Oncall: Actioning: cordon + drain the 26 affected nodes in eu-west. Provision team runbook step: rebuild DKMS modules on target kernel or reprovision nodes with the kernel image matching drivers.
Maria: Logs from one drained node: ```Container runtime error: failed to start container: OCI runtime create failed: container_linux.go:345: starting container process caused: process_linux.go:495: rlimit: file size: value too large``` Not sure how that ties in.
Ajay: Could be an incompatibility in glibc between image and host kernel settings. Another sign we shouldn't mix major distro/kernel baselines when doing toolkit upgrades.
Lisa: We're losing a small handful of v100 nodes to this; suggest we mark V100 pools as "hold" for toolkit12 until we validate DKMS + kernel matrix.
Kai: I'll update our compatibility matrix: kernel versions vs driver vs toolkit vs libc/libstdc++. Also add a test that runs `nvidia-smi --query` on startup and fails fast if mismatch.
SRE-Oncall: For immediate recovery: 1) Pause autoscale, 2) Rollback GPU node image to gold, 3) Rebuild container images with explicit libstdc++ pins, 4) Re-run auto-provision once DKMS rebuilt.
Maria: Pushing a postmortem stub to incidents once we stabilize. Can someone grab cost tags for the runaway capacity window? Need to ask finance for an internal chargeback override.
Ajay: I'll pull the cost dashboard and snapshot the delta. Also setting an alert for toolkit mismatch signatures so we can block image promotion in CI.
infra-bot: [deploy-bot] 1967894689 - Rollback redeploy of redwood/serve:cu11-stable-2026-03-18 initiated by Ajay.
Lisa: After rollback one workload recovered. Still watching for residual NCCL peer errors.
Kai: Long term: add a matrix test harness that boots a tiny VM with each kernel we run in prod, installs drivers, loads DKMS modules, and runs a smoke nvidia-smi + small NCCL allreduce. Failures should stop image promotion.
SRE-Oncall: Adding runbook note: when upgrading toolkit major versions, coordinate kernel freeze for host images or schedule DKMS module rebuild window; do not rollout during cross-region kernel drift.
Maria: Good. Thanks team — keep thread updated with any stuck pods or new errors. I'll schedule a quick postmortem sync in 1h. :thumbsup:
